newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK yacht club could invite China leader as patron.
newsitem.headline: HK yacht club could invite China leader as patron.

text.p: The Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club, regarded by some as a bastion of colonialism, might have to bow to the reality of the colony's return to China by inviting the Chinese head of state to be its patron after the handover.

Queen Elizabeth II is currently the club's patron. But the transfer of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 is likely to change all of that because the post is traditionally taken up by the head of state, which would be Chinese President Jiang Zemin after the handover.
Yacht club vice-commodore Lowell Chang told Reuters the club would discuss the matter in a meeting on Monday. "It's quite a natural move," he said.
Chang said Hong Kong's future leader and former shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa would likely be asked to become the vice-patron, a post traditionally taken up by the governor of Hong Kong.

The club is now a rarity in Hong Kong since it still has the "royal" tag attached to its title. Last May, members voted to keep the attachment for the second time in under a year despite fears that it would antagonise the territory's future master.
The title was granted by Queen Victoria under a royal charter in 1894.
Symbols of British colonialism in Hong Kong are fading fast at the approach of the sovereignty transfer at midnight on June 30 when more than 150 years of British rule comes to an end.
The Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club's sister clubs -- the Hong Kong Jockey Club and the Hong Kong Golf club -- have all abandoned their royal titles.
Some people in the club had expressed fears that the Chinese navy would be less keen to render emergency help to members of an organisation linked with the colonial regime.
The Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club, which has about 3,000 members, will hold another meeting next month to decide whether to keep the royal attachment.
